subject: Human Evolution
title: Creole Languages as Clues
description: A short lesson to help you apply Creole Languages as Clues.

hook.text: When adults speaking different languages meet, they create a pidgin—simple, broken, grammarless.

buildup.text: But when children grow up hearing a pidgin, they spontaneously invent grammar. The result is a creole.

discovery.text: Derek Bickerton argued creolization mirrors how full language first emerged from proto-language.

twist.text: Children don't just learn language—they actively build grammar when none is provided to them.

climax.text: This suggests grammar-building is biologically wired, not just culturally inherited.

punchline.text: Kids don't just learn grammar. They create it.

quiz.question: What happens when children grow up hearing a pidgin language?
options: They spontaneously create grammatical structure, forming a creole
